Show, list and copy table styles

Source: R/tables.R
jstyle.Rd

A style holds a table's look and a journal's or a report's conventions: the font, the caption's form, the rules, the decimals, and for each table type its columns and labels. jstyle() lists the styles jstats can find; jstyle("myjournal") checks a style file and prints every setting the style gives, marking each one it takes from another style; and jstyle("apa", save.as = "myjournal") saves a copy as a style file, myjournal.jstyle, every setting written out with a note on what it does and what it takes, to edit in any text editor (the step SPSS calls "Save TableLook As").

Usage

jstyle(style = NULL, save.as = NULL, overwrite = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

style

The style's name in quotes, or a path to a style file; NULL (the default) lists the styles, or with save.as copies joptions(style = ).

save.as

A name for the copy, in quotes: written as <name>.jstyle in the style folder when one is set, else in your jstats folder (tools::R_user_dir("jstats")), or to a path given with a folder.

overwrite

Logical. Replace a style file that exists? With FALSE (the default) an interactive session asks, and one that cannot ask stops.

...

Settings for a short copy, with save.as: a general setting by its name (font = "Arial"), a table type's settings in a list named for its section (regression = list(fit.rows = "r2")). jstyle_settings lists them all. Any other input stops with "unused input".

Value

Invisibly: the styles found (a data frame of name and path), the style, or the path of the file written.

Details

Given settings, jstyle(save.as =) writes a short file instead: the style it copies named on its based.on line, and only the settings given, which is all a small change needs. A general setting is given by its name; a table type's settings go in a list named for its section: jstyle("apa", save.as = "myapa", font = "Arial", regression = list(fit.rows = c("r2", "n"))).

A style file is plain text: a setting is a name, an equals sign and a value; a # starts a note; the general settings come first, then one section per table type, [descriptives], [frequencies], [regression], [logistic], [correlation], [ttest], [anova], [crosstab] and [reliability]. A setting the file leaves out comes from the style its based.on line names. jstyle_settings lists every setting and what it takes. jstats looks for a style named in a call in the style folder (joptions(style.dir = )), the working directory and your jstats folder, in that order.

See also

jtable for the tables, jstyle_settings for every setting a style holds.

Examples

# The styles jstats can find, and the folders it looks in
jstyle()
#> Styles
#>   apa  built into jstats (the default)
#> 
#> jstats looks for a style file in these folders, in this order:
#>   /home/runner/work/jstats/jstats/docs/reference (the working directory)
#>   /home/runner/.local/share/R/jstats (your jstats folder, not created yet)
#> 

# Every setting of the built-in style
jstyle("apa")
#> Style: apa
#>   built into jstats
#> 
#> font             = Times New Roman
#> size             = 12
#> paper            = a4
#> caption.form     = apa

# A complete copy to edit, and a short one holding two changes
jstyle("apa", save.as = file.path(tempdir(), "myjournal"), overwrite = TRUE)
#> Style written to /tmp/RtmpS2VjTu/myjournal.jstyle
#> 
jstyle("apa", save.as = file.path(tempdir(), "myapa"), overwrite = TRUE,
       font = "Arial", regression = list(fit.rows = c("r2", "n")))
#> Style written to /tmp/RtmpS2VjTu/myapa.jstyle
#>
